PullRequest.Title: Add badge to extensions in customizations

Scenarios.Scenario: Render the Sessions-window Customizations navigation entry and its extension-suggestion badge
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When the Customizations treatment is visible, the navigation-row observables read showBadge; this filters the already-loaded local extension models and inspects manifest contribution keys before the icon/accessible label can settle. The extension workbench service was already registered eager before this PR, so its installed-extension initialization is not newly placed on this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing eager ExtensionsWorkbenchService initialization queries installed extensions through extension-management services.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initialization per Sessions window, independent of the number of badge consumers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The Sessions window already eagerly initialized this service for extension auto-update behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initialization already occurred before the diff and is asynchronous; badge reads use the current in-memory local model and update after onChange.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the dismissed-extension identifier array from profile storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One storage lookup when the delayed suggestion service is first instantiated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous lookup from the storage service's loaded state precedes the first badge computation; no per-extension I/O occurs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Log the experiment trigger through telemetry when eligible suggestions make behavior diverge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one event per telemetry service/window because logExperimentTrigger deduplicates treatment names.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This experiment trigger did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The call is on badge computation, but downstream telemetry delivery is buffered/off the UI critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: O(E × C) over installed non-built-in extensions E and each manifest's contribution keys C; one shared suggestions derived value serves the simultaneous badge consumers while observed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous observable recomputation on the UI thread; extension-change events are transactionally propagated and no parallel boundary fan-out is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The shared suggestions derived caches while badge observers are attached and invalidates on extension-workbench changes or relevant configuration changes. Dismissed identifiers are loaded once from profile storage. There is no cold network cache introduced for badge computation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed observable path, eager pre-existing extension service registration, shared derivation, and one-time telemetry deduplication are directly established by code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installed-extension and manifest sizes vary, but realistic cardinality is bounded and the scan performs in-memory object inspection rather than per-extension I/O.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR intentionally adds one cached in-memory scan to support an always-visible badge; it neither introduces boundary fan-out nor activates the already-eager extension subsystem.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Extensions customization section, render/search its groups, and dismiss the badge
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Navigation calls dismissBadge before the pending section render. Rendering reads the cached suggestion set, groups and sorts installed extensions, and updates the virtualized tree. Search continues to use the existing 200 ms delay; the PR adds a third group and suggestion-membership checks.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the dismissed identifier array in profile storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one write on section navigation or a visible extension-change batch when at least one previously unseen suggestion is added; no write when the set size is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening this section did not persist suggestion-dismissal state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Array creation/serialization occurs before dismissBadge returns; storage persistence is delegated to the existing storage service. The expected payload is proportional to installed-extension history.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Extension installation/uninstallation that produces the existing IExtensionsWorkbenchService onChange event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing extension-management operation cardinality; the diff adds in-memory recomputation and only conditionally adds one profile-storage write for a new suggestion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The widget already rerendered from the same extension-workbench event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The install/uninstall boundary exists independently; the changed render runs after its event and does not add another install query.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: O(E × C) suggestion classification plus O(E log E) grouping/sorting for E installed extensions; a non-empty search can perform the pre-existing second grouping pass. Dismissal serializes D identifiers, where D is the cumulative set dismissed by this profile.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All classification, grouping, and tree-model updates are serialized on the UI thread. One extension-change event schedules one immediate render while visible; no subprocess or network concurrency is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Suggestion classification is cached by the shared derived observable while other badge consumers observe it. The render copies current suggestions into a Set for O(1) group membership. Dismissal skips storage when no new identifier is added, but retained dismissed identifiers are not pruned; expected extension-install history keeps this small enough that no concrete user-visible performance impact is established.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the render and dismissal call order, scan/sort multiplicity, delayed search, and guarded storage write are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Profiles with extreme long-term extension churn could grow the dismissal array, but no realistic size or demonstrated latency/memory consequence supports a high-confidence finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added CPU and storage work is bounded to installed extensions/new suggestions, uses set membership and no-write fast paths, and does not add per-extension I/O.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Agent Customizations management and update contributed-section badges
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Editor sidebar creation registers one autorun. It resolves badge observables once per active harness, reads each management section's badge, and re-splices the short section list only when a badge value actually changes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: O(S) over configured management sections on editor creation or harness change; one O(S) list splice/render for an actual badge transition. S is a small product-defined list, not user history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous observable/list work on the UI thread with no asynchronous fan-out. Harness changes serialize through the observable transaction.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The outer derived caches the section-to-observable mapping per active harness; each badge observable remains observed only while current. updateSectionBadge compares the prior value and avoids redundant list reconstruction.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed autorun, equality guard, list splice, and fixed management-section source are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact list-render cost is unmeasured, but cardinality is product-bounded and updates occur only on badge/harness changes, not per frame or input event.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The work is bounded, change-gated, disposed with editorDisposables, and does not cross filesystem, IPC, database, subprocess, or network boundaries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show suggestion descriptions in hovers and accessibility help
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Hover registrations are created only while a badge is visible and are disposed when the autorun reruns or the widget render store is cleared. Accessibility help performs a one-off suggestion read when explicitly opened.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work per badge hover target; accessibility help may perform one O(E × C) in-memory scan if no observer currently caches suggestions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI work only; no queues or parallel operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Hover disposables are scoped to MutableDisposable/reader.store. The accessibility read uses the derived value, which is cached when observed elsewhere and otherwise intentionally computes once without retaining dependencies.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: lifecycle ownership and one-off read sites are explicit in the changed code and observable implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The accessibility command is infrequent and installed-extension counts vary, but there is no evidence of a hot repeated invocation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. No leak, repeated hot-path work, or boundary operation is introduced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 23 changed files and all diff pages. Traced startup/navigation rendering, extension-change rerenders, dismissal persistence, management-editor badge updates, hover/accessibility lifecycles, telemetry, and extension-management boundaries. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was found, and the PR does not itself fix a proven shipped performance regression.
